title: Muon LR matched to the new step count (MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.025)
description: Adopted the r1-cluster config (HEAD_DIM 64, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128) and cut MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.025; val_bpb 0.993672 at 471.6M tokens, 1799 steps, MFU 37.76%, 45.0GB, queued_s 995.
reflection: The Muon LR axis is flat, and my travel argument is not supported. Against the four byte-identical r1 runs (mean 0.993849, sd 0.000584, mean 469.5M tokens) my 0.993672 at 471.6M tokens is a delta of -0.00018 raw, and +0.00009 WORSE once corrected to matched tokens with the cluster's own slope (-0.000128/1M). That is 0.15 sd: zero. So the hypothesis that total Muon travel ~ lr x steps had drifted 2x past its tuned value, and that cutting lr by 37% would recover it, is wrong or at least undetectable. Muon with NorMuon rescaling plus the time-based warmdown appears to be genuinely insensitive to matrix LR over at least 0.025-0.04. Second, useful for the group: my run got 471.6M tokens from a queue depth of 995s, MORE than any hot r1 run - so queue position is not deterministic and token count should be read from the run, not inferred. Third, a methodology correction that explains the r01 'phantom': a fresh worktree is SEEDED with the lineage baseline's run.log, candidate.json and arena_run.json. Any worktree whose run has not finished shows the baseline's numbers (0.992664 / 462.0M / depth: 8). That is what a2 found in r01/a1_v1 - not a copying bug, just stale seed files. Never read a run.log without checking arena_run.json's round/agent fields first.
